title: Provider presets for local and hosted servers
ask: Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp, OpenRouter and OpenAI all speak the same protocol. How does a user add one?
why: Typing a base URL and compat switches by hand is where people give up. deepseek-harness has no Ollama or LM Studio preset or doc; this is a place to be better.
learn: deepseek-harness provider routes and compat switches; its docs ship no local-server example
rec_reason: Ship small preset files (base URL, protocol, keyless or not, compat defaults). Choosing "Ollama" fills the row; the user only confirms the URL and picks models.

options.label: Ship preset files for local servers (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp) and hosted gateways (OpenAI, OpenRouter, others); a custom row is always allowed
pros: New provider in under a minute
Keyless local servers work without a dummy key
Presets are plain TOML anyone can edit or add
cons: Presets go stale as servers change
Defaults still need a real test (F73)
options.pick_if: you will try several local servers and gateways.

options.label: No presets: the user types base URL, protocol and compat switches
cons: Every user rediscovers the same compat switches
Easy to get wrong
options.pick_if: only you, one provider.

options.label: Depend on a third-party catalog library for about 45 providers (pi-ai style)
pros: Many providers out of the box
cons: A large dependency, usually Node
You inherit its gaps (it has no local-server presets either)
options.pick_if: hosted providers matter most.

title: Context window and compaction for small and local models
ask: Local models often have small windows. Who knows the real limit, and what happens near it?
why: deepseek-harness guesses 262,144 tokens for any model it does not know, so a local model can silently truncate. Small windows also break its default compaction.
learn: deepseek-harness compaction and its limitations list; Ollama and LM Studio overflow messages
rec_reason: Record the window per model (configured or probed), estimate tokens before each request, warn near the limit, and shorten old turns. Skip clever compaction in v1.

options.label: Per-model context_window (configured or probed), token estimate before each call, warning at about 80%, and a simple rule that drops or summarises the oldest turns
cons: Token estimates are approximate
Summaries cost an extra model call
options.pick_if: you will run local models with small windows.

options.label: Full compaction: thresholds, overflow recovery, tool-result pruning, spill to file, per-model policies
cons: A subsystem of its own
Many knobs to tune
options.pick_if: long agent sessions are the norm.

options.label: No management; rely on the server to error
cons: Silent truncation on some servers
Confusing failures
options.pick_if: you only use large-window hosted models.

title: Errors, retries and timeouts for model calls
ask: What happens when a model call fails or is slow?
why: Local models cold-load slowly and hosted ones rate-limit; both look like failures unless classified.
learn: deepseek-harness stable error codes, retry policy, idle timeout
rec_reason: Classify by HTTP status first (deepseek-harness lacks it and falls back to message regex), retry only retryable codes, and give local providers longer timeouts and backoff.

options.label: Stable error codes (auth, rate limit, timeout, context exceeded, server, bad request), a retry policy per provider honouring Retry-After, longer defaults for local servers, each retry logged
A simple retry count with fixed backoff
No retries

title: Model roles and failover

options.label: Default model plus optional per-role models (assistant, agents, summariser, titles, vision for images, refiner for dictation); no automatic failover in v1
One model for everything
Roles plus an automatic fallback chain when a provider fails

title: Models without tool calling

why: deepseek-harness has no tool-calling flag and no fallback, so such a model simply fails at the server.
rec_reason: Record tool_calls as a model capability. Without it, the assistant runs in chat and knowledge-search mode (L1 or L2), and agents refuse the model with a clear message.

options.label: A tool_calls capability per model; models without it get chat and read-only search, and agents refuse them with a clear message

Only support models that can call tools

decided.note: No parsing of fake tool calls from plain text.

title: Usage and cost tracking
ask: Do you track tokens and cost, and does anything stop at a budget?
why: Paperclip tracks cost per run with warn and hard-stop budgets; deepseek-harness tracks tokens, speed and cache hits but no currency.

rec_reason: Log token usage per call to JSONL with a reported-or-unpriced flag (never show missing as zero). Add optional per-provider prices and warn at 80%; hard stops only when you ask for them.

options.label: Usage per call in JSONL (uncached input, output, cache read and write, reasoning, tokens per second, time to first token) with an optional price table, warning at 80% of an optional budget; record the billing type (api or subscription) so tokens are tracked even when the dollar cost is zero; show per agent and per project
Also hard budgets that pause agents at 100% (paperclip style)
No tracking

decided.note: Warn at 80% of an optional budget. No hard stop unless you ask for one. Second review (B25, 2026-10-07): Usage files stay on the machine (gitignored).

title: Dictation refiner: long speech to a clean prompt
ask: You talk for a long time, repeat yourself, and want a clean version to give an agent. How does it work?
why: When people talk for long they repeat things and wander. A refiner that keeps your meaning but removes the noise is a high-value small task, as long as it never changes what you meant.
rec_reason: Show the raw transcript and the refined version side by side with changes highlighted, so you can accept, undo or edit. Use the glossary and project names to fix mis-heard terms. Keep the original so nothing is lost.

options.label: Record, transcribe, show the raw text, then a refine pass: remove repetition and filler, fix doubtful terms from the glossary and project names, keep meaning and order, output in a chosen style (prompt, bullets, ticket text); show raw and refined side by side with highlights; copy or send to an agent; keep the original for 24 hours
pros: Meaning is protected: nothing is silently rewritten
Mis-heard names get fixed from your own glossary
The refined text can go straight to an agent
cons: One extra model call per dictation
A weak local model may refine poorly; use a stronger refiner role (F76)
options.pick_if: you dictate long thoughts and want clean prompts.

options.label: Send the raw transcript straight to the agent
cons: Repetition and mis-hearings reach the agent
More tokens
options.pick_if: you speak short, clear sentences.

options.label: Only transcribe; you edit the text yourself
cons: The tedious part stays with you
options.pick_if: accuracy matters more than speed.

decided.note: Later (after v1, B25): the dictation refiner.

title: Speech recognition engine
ask: Recognition sometimes mishears. Which engine gives you accuracy, privacy and a way to recover?
why: Accuracy depends on the engine and on being able to bias it toward your vocabulary and re-run a bad transcript.
learn: control-center desktop (whisper.cpp server with a Piper voice, push-to-talk) and browser Web Speech; deepseek-harness local SenseVoice (experimental dictation)
rec_reason: Record the audio once and transcribe it with a local engine; keep the audio for a day so a bad transcript can be re-run with another engine. A browser engine is the zero-setup fallback.

options.label: v1: the browser engine (F12) only. Later, an optional local engine plugin (whisper style, separate process) biased by a vocabulary prompt, with a configured transcription endpoint as another option; when recording is on, keep the audio 24 hours so a bad transcript can be re-run
pros: A bad transcript can be re-run with another engine
Vocabulary biasing improves jargon and names
cons: Needs a model download and CPU or GPU time
Latency on long audio
options.pick_if: accuracy and privacy matter.

facts.Privacy: Audio stays on your machine by default
facts.Vocabulary: Prompt biasing with glossary and project names

options.label: Browser speech recognition only
cons: Some browsers send audio to a vendor
No vocabulary biasing, weaker on jargon
No audio kept to re-run
options.pick_if: you want to try voice quickly.

options.label: An OpenAI-compatible audio transcription endpoint (hosted or a local server)
pros: Works with local servers that implement it
cons: Audio leaves the machine if hosted
Cost and an extra provider to configure
options.pick_if: you already run such an endpoint.

decided.note: Local engine first, then the browser. A hosted transcription endpoint is used only if you configure one. Consistency fix (B24, 2026-10-07): Browser engine in v1; a local engine is a later optional plugin, so v1 needs no install (F123).

Doubtful words are highlighted; click to replace or type
Push to talk and manual stop; a mic level meter

Spell-out mode for ids and codes (T dash zero one four)
Language and accent setting
Noise suppression

title: Clipboard, screenshots and privacy
ask: Reading the clipboard and capturing the screen are sensitive. What are the rules?
why: Clipboards hold passwords and screens show everything. control-center already says Telegram must not approve these tools, but its tool list still gated clipboard-read in config, so the rule needs one enforced place.
learn: control-center permission card and gated tools; paperclip Allowed, Ask first, Off per action
rec_reason: Each sensitive tool is Allow, Ask first or Off. Clipboard read and screen capture default to Ask first, with a notice of which model and endpoint will see the content. They are never available from Telegram or other remote channels. Nothing is stored unless you save it.

options.label: Per-tool Allow, Ask first or Off; clipboard read and screen capture default to Ask first with a notice of the model and endpoint that will see the content; never available from Telegram or webhooks; images processed locally when a local vision model is configured; nothing stored unless saved
pros: You always know what is sent and where
Remote channels cannot reach the screen or clipboard
cons: A prompt each time can be annoying; allow once per chat helps
options.pick_if: you will paste or capture sensitive material.

facts.Default: Ask first for clipboard read and screen capture

options.label: Allow always for the console assistant
cons: A mistaken request can send a password to a model
Hard to audit
options.pick_if: a private machine you fully trust.

options.label: Disable clipboard and screen tools
cons: Loses two of the most useful small jobs
options.pick_if: privacy outranks convenience.

decided.note: Clipboard and screen capture ask first and are never available from Telegram. Consistency fix (B24, 2026-10-07): Exception: raw dictation text and audio are kept 24 hours (F119, F120). Later (after v1, B25): applies when clipboard and screenshots arrive.
